text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER DUTY - SEV2: multiple nodes in inference-pool-us-west-2 reporting NotReady and kubelet restarts. alert count: 6. auto-escalating to eng-oncall.
Alice M.: i'm on it — quick triage now. initial symptom looks like kubelet crashes across nodes in the pool.
Ben C.: saw kernel oom messages earlier on uw2-A/B. suspect driver/kernel mem pressure, maybe NVIDIA processes getting oom_killed.
Alice M.: running quick node check, pasting `kubectl get nodes -o wide` snapshot: 
```
NAME                 STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
node-uw2-21          Ready      <none>   45d   v1.26.3
node-uw2-22          NotReady   <none>   46d   v1.26.3
node-uw2-23          NotReady   <none>   30d   v1.26.3
node-uw2-24          NotReady   <none>   12d   v1.26.3
node-uw2-25          Ready      <none>   50d   v1.26.3
```
Carla R.: i'm shifting traffic off that pool now — enabling routing fallback to fallback-us-west-2. we'll drop weight gradually to avoid cold-starts.
infra-sre: grabbed kubelet logs from node-uw2-23, snippet: 
```
Mar 14 12:19:31 node-uw2-23 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 3245 (nvidia-persist) total-vm:...
Mar 14 12:19:31 node-uw2-23 systemd[1]: Started Recreate Volatile Files and Directories...
Mar 14 12:19:32 node-uw2-23 kubelet[1234]: E0314 12:19:32 kubelet.go:987] node not ready: kubelet stopped posting status: runtime status error: failed to start k8s runtime: failed to allocate GPU memory
```
Alice M.: cordoning the worst offenders and starting drains. command i'm running: `kubectl cordon node-uw2-23 && kubectl drain node-uw2-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Ben C.: note: drains will reduce capacity. i'm scaling fallback pool to absorb: `redwoodctl capacity adjust --pool fallback-us-west-2 --replicas +2` (doing now).
pagerduty-bot: @oncall-next assigned for second-line.
oncall-next: i'll take over in ~15m, please add any outstanding actions. is there customer impact?
Alice M.: impact = increased latency and some 502/503 for heavy generation endpoints. not a full failover, but customer-facing errors reported by two enterprise tenants. status page update posted: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/us-west-node-flap
Carla R.: opening support tickets for affected customers. drafting message: "We're investigating node instability in us-west affecting some inference requests; mitigations in progress. No data loss, we may see elevated latencies/503s." will paste to #support after review.
infra-sre: root-cause hypothesis = memory leak in NVIDIA driver 530.x under certain workload patterns causing OOM and kubelet crash. older driver 525 validated in canary. plan: reimage nodes to ami with driver 525 and reboot.
Ben C.: remediation plan: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes 2) taint them NoSchedule 3) reimage/roll nodes to ami-driver-525 4) uncordon gradually and monitor 5) if issues persist, shift more traffic to dedicated fallback pool.
Alice M.: started drain on node-uw2-23 — eviction shows 3 inference pods stuck terminating. `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-uw2-23` output: 
```
inference-gen-abc123   Terminating   0/3   node-uw2-23
inference-kv-xyz789   Terminating   0/2   node-uw2-23
inference-mux-444aaa  Terminating   0/1   node-uw2-23
```
infra-sre: tainting node to stop new scheduling: `kubectl taint nodes node-uw2-23 flapping=true:NoSchedule` — doing for node-uw2-22/23/24.
Ben C.: also increasing autoscaling headroom on fallback pool and enabling burst capacity: `redwoodctl route set --pool fallback-us-west-2 --weight 40%` then monitor latency SLOs.
oncall-next: taking over. i'm going to watch metrics/dashboards and watch for new PagerDuty alerts. please drop any final handoff notes here.
Alice M.: handoff notes:
- nodes 22/23/24 experienced kubelet restarts due to OOM of NVIDIA driver processes
- drained and tainted; reimage queued to ami-driver-525 (patch rollout plan in infra-runbook)
- routing adjusted to fallback-us-west-2 to absorb load; scaling +2 replicas triggered
- customer comms in progress for two tenants; support tickets opened (#T-451, #T-452)
- monitoring: token-level latency increased ~30% for gen-large models, error rate up ~0.8% on affected routes
Carla R.: customer-facing template sent to #support. also created internal incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/7892 (SRE ticket 7892).
oncall-next: thanks — i'm running the rollout plan now and will keep thread pinned. if anything changes, ping me @oncall-next. leaving initial triage notes in incident doc and will update root cause when reimages finish.
incident-bot: Incident 7892 status updated -> mitigated; monitoring. :white_check_mark:
